subject: Materials Science
title: Tensile Testing: The Universal Test
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Tensile Testing: The Universal Test.

hook.text: Grab both ends of a dog-bone shaped specimen and pull until it breaks — that's a tensile test.

buildup.text: A universal testing machine grips the specimen and pulls at a controlled rate while recording force and extension.

discovery.text: The result is a stress-strain curve — from it you read modulus, yield, UTS, and ductility.

twist.text: The dog-bone shape ensures failure happens in the narrow gauge section — not at the grips.

climax.text: Every batch of structural steel, every titanium lot for implants, is tensile-tested before use.

punchline.text: Pull it until it breaks — and learn everything about the material.

quiz.question: What does a tensile test measure?
options: Only the hardness of the material
Stress-strain behavior including modulus, yield, and ductility
The chemical composition of the material
